chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ulwan narrated from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, in Paradise there is a tree from whose top garments come forth, and from its bottom come horses of mixed black and white, saddled, bridled, and winged, that neither defecate nor urinate. They are mounted by the friends of Allah, and they fly with them in Paradise wherever they wish. So those who are below them will say, 'Our Lord, what has brought Your servants to this nobility?' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, 'Verily, they used to stand [in prayer] at night and not sleep, and fast during the day and not eat, and fight the enemy and not be cowardly, and give charity and not be miserly.'

key_terms.خَيْلٌ بُلْقٌ: Horses of mixed black and white color

ai.seo_question: What are the specific acts of worship and virtues that grant the friends of God the ability to fly on winged horses in Paradise?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the eschatological reward for the *Awliya* (Friends of God), linking their spiritual elevation to a specific combination of night prayer (*Qiyam*), daytime fasting, and steadfast jihad. The imagery of winged, pure horses symbolizes the transcendence of the soul, while the divine explanation emphasizes that this status is earned through consistent devotion and generosity without stinginess, reflecting key Shia virtues of asceticism and piety.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 7.Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUlwān narrated from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī (a) who said,

“Verily there is a tree in Paradise from the top of which [paradisal] garments come forth, and from the bottom of which come horses of mixed black and white colour, saddled, bridled, and with  wings, that neither defecate or urinate. They are mounted by the friends of Allah who fly with them wherever they wish in Paradise, so those who are below them will say, ‘Our Lord, what made these servants of Yours reach such a noble station?’ So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say, ‘They would stand up [to worship] in the night and would not sleep, they would fast during the day and not eat, they would fight the enemy and were not cowardly, and they would give charity and were not miserly.’”
